batchName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284) - Hard Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284)

questions.question: Where did Septimius Severus's last rival in the civil wars fall in 197?
questions.explanation: Severus's last rival fell at Lugdunum, modern Lyon, in 197, ending four years of civil war. Severus then turned against the Parthians.
questions.sourceQuote: His last rival fell at Lugdunum, modern Lyon, in 197.

questions.question: Which later ruler modelled her coin portraits on the Severan empresses?
questions.explanation: Decades later, the Syrian queen Zenobia copied the Severan empresses on her coins. Julia Domna's family power had outlived her through her sister and nieces.
questions.sourceQuote: Decades later, the Syrian queen Zenobia would model her coin portraits on these Severan empresses.

questions.question: Septimius Severus cut the silver content of the denarius from 81.5% to what?
questions.explanation: Severus reduced the silver from 81.5% to 78.5%. The Severans also enlarged the army by a quarter and doubled legionaries' pay.
questions.sourceQuote: The Severans enlarged the army by a quarter and doubled legionaries' pay; Septimius Severus cut the silver in the denarius, Rome's standard coin, from 81.5% to 78.5%.

questions.question: Roughly how many men won the Senate's recognition as emperor during the Crisis of the Third Century?
questions.explanation: About 26 men were recognised by the Senate, while over 50 claimed the title. All but one recognised emperor died violently.
questions.sourceQuote: About 26 men won the Senate's recognition as emperor, and over 50 claimed the title.

questions.question: By when had Aurelian made the Roman Empire whole again by destroying the Gallic Empire?
questions.explanation: After Palmyra surrendered in August 272, Aurelian destroyed the Gallic Empire, so by late 274 the empire was reunited. He also reformed the coinage before being assassinated in 275.
questions.sourceQuote: Aurelian then destroyed the Gallic Empire, so by late 274 the empire was whole, and he reformed the coinage.

questions.question: Stories of Zenobia's cowardice in defeat were most likely the product of what?
questions.explanation: Tales of her cowardice were probably Aurelian's propaganda. Sources like the Historia Augusta also reshaped her image to flatter favoured emperors.
questions.sourceQuote: Tales of her cowardice in defeat were probably Aurelian's propaganda.

questions.question: Which acts of the emperor known as Elagabalus are confirmed by coins and inscriptions? (select all that apply)
options: He executed his cousin and heir
He placed his god above Jupiter
He moved the capital to Emesa
questions.explanation: Coins and inscriptions confirm that in 220 he ranked his god above Jupiter and that he married a Vestal Virgin. The claim that he was Caracalla's son comes only from one account, and he merely tried to kill his cousin.
questions.sourceQuote: Coins and inscriptions confirm that in 220 he placed his god above Jupiter, and that he married a Vestal Virgin (*virgo Vestalis*), a priestess sworn to chastity.

questions.question: What did Zenobia do in 272 that marked an open break with Rome?
options: Minted coins of the emperor beside her son
questions.explanation: With a Roman army approaching in 272, Zenobia declared herself empress. Earlier she had minted coins showing the Roman emperor beside her son.
questions.sourceQuote: But in 272, with a Roman army approaching, she declared herself empress, an open break with Rome.

questions.question: What happened to Caracalla's praetorian-prefect successor in 218? (select all that apply)
options: He was executed by the Senate in Rome
He was killed by his guards while fleeing
He was captured by the Parthians
He died of natural causes in Syria
He was killed in battle at Emesa
questions.explanation: After troops in Syria hailed a teenage Severan in May 218, Macrinus was defeated near Antioch, caught as he fled and killed by his guards. He had never set foot in Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: The usurper was defeated near Antioch, the great city of Roman Syria, caught as he fled, and killed by his guards.

questions.question: Where and when was Caracalla murdered?
questions.explanation: Caracalla was murdered near Carrhae, in modern south-eastern Turkey, in April 217 while heading to fight the Parthians. The killing was ordered by one of his own guard commanders.
questions.sourceQuote: In April 217, heading to fight the Parthians, he was murdered near Carrhae, a town in modern south-eastern Turkey, on the orders of one of his own guard commanders.
